Round: the side-by-side list answer, and the report record.

Read against origin/main 19f3733 — after #56, so the rail frame, the four states and the member-tree link are already built. This draws the half that is still open: the rail SENTENCE, and where a saved list lives.

#60 has since built the sentence — see REVIEW-RAIL-SENTENCE.md for the three copy defects.
The two numbers agree out loud: 32 in the rail, 32 in the pane, and "10 of 32 packed" says what the model actually saw. That clause is the provenance of the sentence beside it, not an apology.
One Record, two kinds. Curate's commit is the catalogue kind and already exists — append-only, server-stamped author, selection as a snapshot. A report is the same row with no steps.

The two calls handed back in FUNNEL-COST-IMPLEMENTED.md: where the wait/background choice goes on /next's one-click re-run, and §3 — keep-investigating offering the deeper surveys with the split price.

Read against main at 2d4357e.

Round one of the ports work. Read against origin/main 91d6d93.

Leads with a correction: the Curate column claims ports are derived from the accepted set. They are not — interfaces.propose() reads deployment artifacts at survey time and never consults a verdict.

And the scale finding: no human-accepted component is cohesive under any bar; curators accept named packages. So review happens at the branch.

The owner's round of 2026-09-14, points 1/2/3/6/7/9/10 — seven faces of one question.

Read against origin/main 0841c17.

The cause, from the code rather than the complaint: the Questions row renders the answer and cannot reach the members; Dashboard by-question renders the SAME sentence from the same envelope so it can host a detail disclosure whose payload opens in a 290px rail.

The owner's second round, 2026-09-15. Read against origin/main 93be502.

Point 3: the honesty rules made a surface scrupulous about what it cannot say and silent about what to do. The missing half is WHOSE absence it is.

Points 4/5/6 are one habit: a row composed from several analyses over several populations, written as though it came from one.

Item 1 of the work plan, ruled. Read against origin/main 05cb63c0 — after #104.

The question was unanswerable because three different things in this product are called "perspective": run_label (detect/coupling), Component.perspective (physical/deployment/logical/dev), and the twelve role chips in the chrome.

Ruling: a verdict is about the component — the thing at that path — not about the proposal that surfaced it. No schema change; four render changes and one sort change.

Item 2 of the work plan — the component branch tree, unblocked by the verdict ruling on page six.

The owner's point 4 is four questions in one: what this is, why we think so, how much of it you are seeing, and what you can do about it. The tree answers all four in the same rows.

Measured figures are from #85 on egeria-workspaces; the five branch rows are illustrative shapes, not spec. The artboard says which is which at the foot — a drawing should carry its own provenance.

Item 3 of the plan. Read against main at 7b7bc2b4.

Two halves. Selection is a control that already exists one level out — selectMode is resource-level in the sidebar; the tree has per-row accept and no way to act on several.

Blueprints are the live defect: the coverage sentence says '0 of 12 clusters in the logical reading reviewed' and blueprints have ZERO UI references in /next. A count that opens nothing.

And a blueprint verdict is reading-scoped (perspective::cluster_name) where a component's is path-scoped — one table, two identity regimes, and the screen has to say which.

Round 2 of the multi-resource brief, drawn against slices 6 and 7 as merged.

Every field name and all four state values are the shipped ones from database_column_profiles. stats_source and stats_computed_at are there because round 1 asked for them — the schema comment quotes the reasoning.

The third panel is not a design question: n_distinct is negative when it expresses a ratio, so the shipped REAL column will render "distinct: −0.8" unless the sign is branched on at the render site. Same shape as the counter-reset case.

Treemap deliberately not drawn — its inventory rows need checking the same way these fields were. The heatmap IS drawn, on page 10: slice 8 had landed in #193, which I only found on looking.

Round 2, second drawing. Read against main at 9d531b3b — slice 8 (postgres_operations, #193) had already landed, so the role side exists and this was drawable after all.

Drawing it found three separate paths by which the grid can say "no access" about a role that has access:

1. Cells are inherited from TABLE grants. role_table_grants is table-level and database_grants has no column_name, so a column-only grant (GRANT SELECT (email)) is invisible. Ask: read information_schema.column_privileges — a strict superset — and add column_name. A migration, which is why it belongs in round 2.

2. PUBLIC is a pseudo-role, so it cannot be one column among five. It is a band above the grid.

3. Role membership is read nowhere — no pg_auth_members, no pg_has_role. Granting through a group role is normal Postgres administration. has_column_privilege() answers all three at once.

The rule the page turns on: for an exposure view the two failure directions are not symmetric. An empty cell must mean "no path found", never "no path".

Round 3. Read against main at 9bc1c153 — slices 9, 10 and 12 merged.

Both round-2 items were fixed, and the n_distinct fix went three corrections deep, catching the reltuples provenance and the PG13 sentinel ambiguity I had not seen.

Two findings:

1. The DRAFT badge is correct in classic, including the part nobody asked for — an empty contentStatus draws no badge because 'not stated' is not 'confirmed'. /next has no Egeria annotation surface at all, so the divergence is permitted today and becomes a silent omission the day that pane is built. And amber cannot port: /next has three audited state roles and no room for a fourth. DRAFT is not a state — it says who has agreed so far, orthogonal to ok/warn/gap — so it is an ink chip, not a colour.

2. The n_distinct fix correctly refuses to guess, returning None — for four different reasons, on a row still labelled state = measured. A wrong number became a blank that cannot say why. The live case: pg_stat_reset() clears last_analyze while pg_stats survives, so after a reset every near-unique column loses its distinct count on a healthy database. stats_reset is already in scope at database_surveyor.py:379 and is not consulted.

Heatmap: wait. The next drawing depends on which of the two grant fixes is taken. But the shipping rule is settleable now — it must not ship caveated, because a caveated exposure grid is still read as a grid.

Designer round 2 on the database screens. Read against main at 019c2796 (#318) and the owner's screenshots of 2026-09-27.

Three things in the screenshots are already fixed in code: tree order, kind words, the filter's expanded-empty table.

The finding under all three items: there are already three glyph tables (GLYPH, factGlyph, CELL) that disagree, and the brief would add a fourth. One table, one module; the glyph names a family, the word names the state.

A prerequisite for the tree overview: 'empty' folds four conditions, including never-measured, stored as row_total 0. A row-count bar built on it draws 'not measured' as 'counted, zero'.

The per-schema overview goes into the tree's rows rather than a second chart, with rows AND columns: column counts come from the catalog, so a structure-only credential still gets a real bar.

Header: each line leads with its state; only the remedy is in the accent colour. Neither remedy exists in /next today.
